dem.name: LOLA south pole, 85S square at 80 m
LOLA south pole, 80S square at 160 m

assumptions: Observer 2 m above the terrain at -84.7900, 29.2000 (degrees, east-positive, ME frame); heights above the 1737.4 km sphere.
Positions are topocentric and airless (no refraction), as JPL Horizons APPARENT=AIRLESS for a coord@301 observer.

Skyline from elevation data, including the Moon's curvature, 0.5 deg in azimuth, searched to 189 km: LOLA LDEM_80S_20M, 60 m site window (60 m) from 0.0 to 5.4 km; LOLA south pole, 85S square at 80 m (80 m) from 3.9 to 130.9 km; LOLA south pole, 80S square at 160 m (160 m) from 13.6 to 175.6 km; LOLA whole-Moon grid, 16 px/deg (1895.21 m) from 165.2 to 188.6 km.
Sampled every 10 min; rise and set times refined to 10 s; the Sun and Earth are discs (visible fraction integrated across each disc).
Sunrise/sunset = first/last moment any part of the Sun stands above the skyline. Earthrise/Earthset = Earth's centre crossing the skyline.
Sunlight also counts Earth passing in front of the Sun (geometric discs; the faint light refracted by Earth's atmosphere is ignored).
Earth visibility is geometric line of sight only; it says nothing about a working radio link.
Slope over a 120 m baseline from LOLA LDEM_80S_20M, 60 m site window, 60 m: hazards smaller than the grid are not seen.

warnings: Elevation data at this point, finest first: LOLA LDEM_80S_20M, 60 m site window (60 m per sample, to about 3.8 km); LOLA south pole, 85S square at 80 m (80 m per sample, to about 14 km); LOLA south pole, 80S square at 160 m (160 m per sample, to about 166 km); LOLA LDEM_80S_20M, 480 m site window (480 m per sample, to about 31 km); LOLA whole-Moon grid, 16 px/deg (1.9 km per sample, whole Moon).
Beyond about 166 km from the site only the whole-Moon grid is available (1.9 km per sample), which smooths ridges narrower than that; distant skyline peaks can read slightly low.
Earth passes in front of the Sun during this window (2025-03-14 04:23 UTC): sunlight and darkness include it.
